status: Uncommitted working study with scoped local review.

assumptions_and_readouts.archive: Five unmodified radius-one carrier preparations have no orientation-ID observations. Site survival has only the definitional 0–1 bound from those data.
assumptions_and_readouts.marked_collar: Constant volume density; smooth 0 to 0.012R displacement in one transit. Passive radial sink plus a decaying potential dipole. beta=0 and 1 compare free redistribution with enforced uniform inner-cut inflow. n(r) is constant for this prescribed incompressible inflow. The full initially filled collar loses Q previous material per unit time until a new entrant reaches the exit. In the half-transit interval of the reported test no entrant could cross the radial thickness, even at the upper bound on inward speed. Front/back survivor fractions are conditioned on initial latitude and cover all initial radii.
assumptions_and_readouts.pulse: The six-site collision experiment uses equally spaced passage times and independent lossless nearest-neighbor encounters. Input after pulse is fresh local ground state; outgoing phase and total surviving complex signal close. The separate, single-entrant time-integrated response has no positive probability interpretation for complex transfer.
assumptions_and_readouts.held_patch: The four-state Wolfram calculation uses a separate Poisson joint replacement process, J=6, field=4, event rate=4, hbar=1, handoff probability 1/2, and field-tracking resets. It tests positive absorption and the distinction between in-phase and conjugate-quadrature measurements, not the residence distribution in the collar.
assumptions_and_readouts.static_and_lane: Six radial layers include the original cut. Per surface angular edge the new product-state energy is J times one minus the squared complete-register overlap. The radial trial costs zero on radial links and at most 24J per angular mesh. The previous static comparison applies to the same admissible class on the original cut with its exterior counted once. The dynamical demonstration uses an isolated held lane, constant exchange and prescribed inward shifts. It is not a coupled quantum annulus or a solution for Q(R).
assumptions_and_readouts.receiver: One two-state face per participating site, uniformly polarized incoming state, imposed gap and radial axis, identical resonant vacuum interaction events, and a readout of the dominant reduced eigenray. At the opposed pole r^k is the excited-state probability and 1−2r^k is polarization along the preferred direction. The initial azimuthal precession-free sign choice is common across the mesh. At equality the ray is undefined. The relative orientation degree is not a calibrated physical charge. A pure state on spin and all receivers is distinct from the preferred receiver Schmidt ray. The spatial prism and the internal joint-state tests are different observables.

independent_local_reviews.verdict: Scoped clear for the final report’s source fidelity on the marked-collar transport, held-lane pulse, product-state energy bound, and one-face preparation and receiver readouts. The report correctly limits the ring prediction to its odd-in-drive component and distinguishes the spatial compensating index from the opposite winding of the collective receiver’s Schmidt partner. The physical angular-link response, distant electric force, and 0PN acceleration remain open. The reviewed report hash matches the manifest.
independent_local_reviews.dispositions: Separated the analytically inferred half-transit global survival from latitude-resolved measurements, specified the odd-in-drive comparison, and identified the dominant reduced direction for an individual receiver. Joint-state topology and the spatial index are separate readouts.

independent_local_reviews.verdict: Scoped clear for source fidelity and the conditional carrier-turnover, angular-memory, preparation-energy, collar-index, and receiver-winding results in `mouth_turnover_and_orientation.md`. No outstanding fixes. Verified the corrected archive and odd-response statements and the manifest's report checksum; physical external electric charge, force, and 0PN acceleration remain open.
independent_local_reviews.scope: Independent archive and checksum audit, derivation of material and orientation observables and final source fidelity.
independent_local_reviews.dispositions: Specified the carried momentum rate and integrated feeding-side stress, initial-latitude survival, matched full/half odd response, supplied preparation and the distinction between material winding and exterior physical charge.
